A developer says simulations from engines like Isaac Sim often fail once deployed on real robotic hardware. They attribute this to GPU execution-order differences in discrete physics steps (collisions, friction, constraints) that accumulate into sim-to-real drift in complex scenarios. They built an audit tool, SIPA, to measure this.

On Isaac GR00T: interesting to see NVIDIA move higher up the AI stack, but the commenter questions its value. 'All of the demos look really slow.' They doubt more training data will fix this and see it as a current limit in physical encoding/decoding of action, especially for humanoids.

Praise for NVIDIA releasing Isaac GR00T N1 under the Apache 2 license, contrasting it with Google's Gemini robotics model, which was not open-sourced. The commenter hopes the release pushes Google to open theirs.
